title: Week 1: The Goose Who Would Be Mayor

cards.text: The Goose Union demands a pond. Inside City Hall. In your office. They've already measured your desk.

right.label: Build the pond
right.reaction: Honk! (Gratitude. Probably.)

left.label: No ponds indoors
left.reaction: The union will remember this. They have long memories and longer necks.

up.label: A pond in the park
up.reaction: A compromise. The geese are... considering it.

cards.text: The pond contractor is a goose. He's laid the foundations. And an egg. Work has stopped.

right.label: Pay him in bread
right.reaction: Work resumed. The egg is supervising.

left.label: Hire human builders
left.reaction: The geese are picketing the humans. The humans are scared.

cards.text: The pond is finished. It's in your office. It's lovely. Except the smell. And the smell's smell.

right.label: Grand opening!
right.reaction: Gerald cut the ribbon. With his face.

left.label: Quiet opening
left.reaction: The geese are hurt you didn't invite the press.

cards.text: The office pond is leaking. Into the records room. 1987 is underwater. 1988 is next.

right.label: Fix the leak
right.reaction: Dry again. 1987 will smell of pond forever.

left.label: Call it an indoor river
left.reaction: Tourists are kayaking through Planning.

cards.text: There is goose poop on every floor of City Hall. Every floor. Including the roof. How?

right.label: Hire cleaners
right.reaction: Clean! For about an hour.

left.label: It's good luck
left.reaction: Marge printed that. Now people want some.

cards.text: The indoor river has reached the library. The books are swimming. Some of them are winning.

right.label: Build a bridge
right.reaction: A bridge inside City Hall. It has a troll. The troll is Randy.

left.label: Sell rafting tickets
left.reaction: Rafting is up. Paperwork is down. Mostly in the river.

cards.text: The geese have had goslings. Forty of them. They'd like a second pond. For the children. Honk.

right.label: A second pond
right.reaction: HONK! (Gerald wept. Then bit Doug.)

left.label: One pond is plenty
left.reaction: The goslings are staging a sit-in. They're very small. It's very sad.

cards.text: The geese have occupied the car park. They have a flag. They have a list. The list is mostly 'pond'.

right.label: Fine, build the pond
right.reaction: Victory honk. The flag stays.

left.label: Send in Chief Barb
left.reaction: Barb versus geese. The geese are winning on points.

cards.text: We've lost the bakery. The geese have the bakery. They're making bread. For themselves.

right.label: Negotiate
right.reaction: Peace. The bread is shared. It's mostly crusts.

left.label: Starve them out
left.reaction: They have a bakery. You cannot starve a bakery.

cards.text: The geese have elected their own mayor. It's Gerald. His approval rating is higher than yours.

right.label: Debate Gerald
right.reaction: He honked for an hour. He won on volume.

left.label: Merge the towns
left.reaction: You're co-mayor with a goose. Honestly, it's going fine.

cards.text: The park pond is nice. But the geese say the park is 'outside'. They would like a roof. A big one.

right.label: Build a roof
right.reaction: A roof over a pond. Indoor-outdoor living. Honk.

left.label: Outside is fine
left.reaction: Gerald wrote an op-ed. It's mostly 'HONK'.

cards.text: Lovely town. How much for all of it? I'm asking for a friend. The friend is me.

right.label: Name a silly price
right.reaction: A billion and a goose. Interesting. I'll be back.

left.label: Throw him out
left.reaction: I've been thrown out of better towns. This one, actually.

up.label: Hear him out
up.reaction: A deposit. No strings. A few strings.

cards.text: About our deal. I'd like the clock tower. Just the clock. Not the tower. Or the time.

right.label: Give him the clock
right.reaction: Nobody knows what time it is. Productivity is way up.

left.label: Return his deposit
left.reaction: Pity. I'll be in touch. Through the basement.

cards.text: A note under your door: 'LOOK IN THE BASEMENT.' The handwriting is very neat. Suspiciously neat.

right.label: Go and look
right.reaction: Boxes. Hundreds. All labelled 'DO NOT COUNT'.

left.label: Burn the note
left.reaction: A second note arrived. It just says 'RUDE.'

cards.text: A third note. It was in your sandwich. 'BASEMENT. PLEASE.' The sandwich was otherwise fine.

right.label: Fine, go and look
right.reaction: Boxes. So many boxes.

left.label: Eat the sandwich
left.reaction: Delicious. Ominous. Delicious.

cards.text: The basement boxes are old ballots from the last election. Every single one says 'Gerald'.

right.label: Tell the town
right.reaction: So the goose won. And nobody said anything.

left.label: Put them back
left.reaction: You saw nothing. The boxes saw you.

cards.text: You found the ballots. I was the mayor before you. They voted for a goose instead. Help me, or expose me.

right.label: Expose him
right.reaction: Print it. I've been run out of better towns.

left.label: Take his hush money
left.reaction: Smart. Wrong, but smart.

cards.text: Technically, I am the mayor. Honk. I'd like my office back. I hear it has a pond now.

right.label: Share the office
right.reaction: Co-mayors. He sits on the desk. You sit near the desk.

left.label: Absolutely not
left.reaction: He's filed a lawsuit. In honk.

cards.text: Main Street has a pothole so big it has a name. The name is Kevin. Kevin got a jury summons.

right.label: Fill in Kevin
right.reaction: Goodbye, Kevin. You were expensive.

left.label: Leave Kevin alone
left.reaction: Kevin is growing. Kevin is thriving.

up.label: Sell tickets to Kevin
up.reaction: People are queuing. To look at a hole.

cards.text: Kevin swallowed a parked car. It was Chad's. Chad would like it back, or Kevin arrested.

right.label: Fish out the car
right.reaction: It smells of hole. Chad sold it to Kevin's fans.

left.label: Arrest Kevin
left.reaction: You arrested a hole. Marge has a front page for a week.

cards.text: Kevin is now a sinkhole. He ate the post office. Kevin is getting mail.

right.label: Fill it with concrete
right.reaction: Kevin is sealed. We can hear him sulking.

left.label: Kevin is an attraction
left.reaction: Two tourists fell in. They're fine. Kevin's fine.

cards.text: Good news: Kevin is filled. Bad news: Kevin Junior has appeared next door. He has his father's eyes.

right.label: Fill him too
right.reaction: Kevin Junior is gone. There are rumours of a Kevin the Third.

left.label: Let the boy grow
left.reaction: Kevin Junior has a fan club. It's Timmy.

cards.text: The Bugle needs a front page. Can we say you wrestled a bear? Not a big bear. A believable bear.

right.label: Yes, I wrestled a bear
right.reaction: Did you win? Never mind. You won.

left.label: Tell the truth
left.reaction: Honesty. On a Tuesday. Bold.

cards.text: A bear is in my office. It read the article. It says you two need to talk.

right.label: Apologise to the bear
right.reaction: The bear accepts. It would like a column.

left.label: Wrestle it for real
left.reaction: You lost. But we got photos.

cards.text: The bear's column is our most popular. It's mostly about honey. Now it wants to run for council.

right.label: Endorse the bear
right.reaction: The bear is on council. It sits on two chairs.

left.label: Bears can't run
left.reaction: The bear is suing. Its lawyer is also a bear.

cards.text: The bear wants a rematch. Live on Town TV. Everyone's betting. Mostly on the bear.

right.label: Accept the rematch
right.reaction: You lost again, bravely. Record ratings.

left.label: Hide in the cheese vault
left.reaction: The bear found you. It brought crackers.

cards.text: Put a casino in the library. Books are just slow slot machines. Think of the revenue. I have.

right.label: Build the casino
right.reaction: You won't regret this. Others will.

left.label: Refuse
left.reaction: Fine. Enjoy your free knowledge.

up.label: One casino night
up.reaction: One night. I'll make it count.

cards.text: Someone is counting cards at the library casino. It's the librarian. She's very good. Chad is crying.

right.label: Ban Linda
right.reaction: She moved to roulette. She's very good at that too.

left.label: Make her head of security
left.reaction: Nobody cheats now. She can smell it.

cards.text: The casino owes money. To Linda. It's the whole casino. She owns it now.

right.label: Let her keep it
right.reaction: The casino is a library again. With better odds.

left.label: Bail it out
left.reaction: Chad thanks you. Linda doesn't.

cards.text: Casino night made a fortune. Everyone wants another. Every night. Starting tonight.

right.label: Every night
right.reaction: The library never sleeps. The librarians are furious.

left.label: Once was enough
left.reaction: Chad is calling it 'a tragedy for culture'.

cards.text: Can we have a Frog Day? I already told everyone there's a Frog Day. Also the frogs. They're coming.

right.label: Frog Day!
right.reaction: FROG DAY! FROG DAY!

left.label: No Frog Day
left.reaction: I'm telling the frogs.

cards.text: Frog Day went well. The frogs have not left. They're in the fountain, the school, and my hat.

right.label: Frog round-up
right.reaction: Rounded up. Two escaped. They're in charge now.

left.label: Frogs are citizens now
left.reaction: The frogs registered to vote. Turnout is excellent.

cards.text: The frogs have endorsed a candidate for mayor. It's a bigger frog.

right.label: Court the frog vote
right.reaction: You ate a fly on camera. Frogs approve.

left.label: Frogs can't vote after all
left.reaction: Timmy is on hunger strike. He had a big breakfast first.

cards.text: The frogs came anyway. They're very disappointed. One of them is crying. It's me. I'm crying.

right.label: Fine, a small Frog Day
right.reaction: Small Frog Day! Small frogs!

left.label: Be strong
left.reaction: Marge photographed Timmy crying. Front page.

cards.text: We need a helicopter. For crime. And also, mostly, for fun. I've already bought the sunglasses.

right.label: Buy it
right.reaction: Front seat. Forever.

left.label: Lease one
left.reaction: A rental. I'm still doing the noises.

down.label: No helicopter
down.reaction: Fine. I'll run very fast with my arms out.

cards.text: The helicopter circles the school all day. The children can't hear the teacher. Grades are up, oddly.

right.label: Ground it in school hours
right.reaction: Barb is sulking in the hangar.

left.label: It's educational
left.reaction: The children are fluent in helicopter.

cards.text: The helicopter is stuck on the church spire. Barb is still in it. She says she lives there now.

right.label: Rescue Barb
right.reaction: Rescued. She's already planning a second helicopter.

left.label: Let her live there
left.reaction: She has a view. She's happy. Crime is unattended.

cards.text: I'm launching a rocket from the school field. My guy says it's safe. My guy says it goes 'mostly up'.

right.label: Clear the launch
right.reaction: Ten, nine, eight...

left.label: No rockets near children
left.reaction: Fine. I'll launch something quieter. And bigger.

cards.text: Chad's rocket went up. It's coming down. My forecast: the library. Or the moon. Probably the library.

right.label: Evacuate the library
right.reaction: Everyone's out. Linda refused. She's fine. Of course she is.

left.label: It'll miss
left.reaction: It did not miss.

cards.text: The rocket landed on the library. The top floor's books are in orbit. Returns are due Friday.

right.label: Rebuild the library
right.reaction: Reopened. In case the books come back.

left.label: Leave the rocket in
left.reaction: It's the reading rocket now. Story time has a countdown.

cards.text: The town needs a mascot. Our readers voted. They chose 'Wet Sock'.

right.label: Welcome, Wet Sock
right.reaction: He's damp. He's proud. He's ours.

left.label: Hire a designer
left.reaction: It's a smiling building. Readers call it 'Dry Sock'.

cards.text: Wet Sock merchandise is selling out. I want a cut. Also a sock. A wet one.

right.label: Give Chad a cut
right.reaction: Damp profits.

left.label: Free socks for the people
left.reaction: Free wet socks for all. Nobody asked for this.

cards.text: Wet Sock dried out in the sun. The children are inconsolable. He's just a sock now.

right.label: Re-wet the sock
right.reaction: He's back. Damper than ever.

left.label: Let him go
left.reaction: A state funeral for a sock. Marge wept.

cards.text: Boss. Small favour. Can I... we... get a pay rise? In bin bags. Not money. Bin bags.

right.label: Bin bags it is
right.reaction: Thank you. Best day of our... my life.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Understood. We'll be in the bins. Sulking.

cards.text: Randy's 'cousins' have moved into City Hall. All of them. They're raccoons. Randy says they're 'consultants'.

right.label: Hire the consultants
right.reaction: Productivity is up. The bins are down.

left.label: Evict them
left.reaction: They left. Randy cried. Three times. Simultaneously.

cards.text: A pigeon has been signing papers at your desk for a week. I checked. Some of it is very good policy.

right.label: Hire the pigeon
right.reaction: It wants an office. The office must have a ledge.

left.label: Evict the pigeon
left.reaction: It left. It took your stapler. It knew which one was yours.

cards.text: The pigeon now has a press secretary. Also a pigeon. They've announced a policy on bread.

right.label: Back the bread policy
right.reaction: Bread for everyone. Mostly crumbs.

left.label: Clip its wings, politically
left.reaction: The pigeon resigned. In a single, dignified coo.

cards.text: Teens are standing near the fountain. Just standing. One of them is leaning. I want a curfew.

right.label: Curfew at 9 pm
right.reaction: Order. Beautiful, quiet order.

left.label: Let them stand
left.reaction: Then I'm standing near them. Menacingly.

up.label: Fund a youth centre
up.reaction: Now they stand indoors. I'll allow it.

cards.text: I'd like a tiny tax break. You'd need a telescope to see it. I own the telescope shop. Telescopes are tax-free now too.

right.label: Grant it
right.reaction: Thank you. I used the savings to buy the tax office. It's a gym now.

left.label: Refuse
left.reaction: I'll remember this. I've hired a man to remember it for me.

cards.text: School lunch is beige. All of it. Yesterday the beige was seen leaving the kitchen on its own.

right.label: Pay for real food
right.reaction: A vegetable! Some of them cried.

left.label: Chad sponsors lunch
left.reaction: 'Chad Nuggets.' The Bugle is having a field day.

down.label: Beige builds character
down.reaction: The PTA has a long memory.

cards.text: The station needs a police dog. We have one. Sergeant Biscuit. He is afraid of crime, cats, and Tuesdays.

right.label: Buy a braver dog
right.reaction: This one bit me. Perfect.

left.label: Therapy for Biscuit
left.reaction: He's talking about his feelings. Barking, really.

cards.text: The town's mimes are on strike. Nobody can tell. They'd like you to notice. They're pointing at you. Hard.

right.label: Notice them loudly
right.reaction: They're thrilled. One is trapped in a box about it.

left.label: Ignore the mimes
left.reaction: They're booing. Silently. It's somehow worse.

cards.text: We could put parking meters on Main Street. People will hate it. But the meters take coins, and I do love the coins.

right.label: Install meters
right.reaction: Coins! Someone parked a horse to avoid paying. It worked.

left.label: Free parking forever
left.reaction: Forever. A man's been parked there since Tuesday. He's put up curtains.

cards.text: The emergency fund is four tons of cheese, stored since 1987. I went down to count it. It counted me back.

right.label: Sell the cheese
right.reaction: Sold. The buyer asked if it 'always hums'. I said yes. I don't know.

left.label: Cheese festival
left.reaction: Nine thousand people. One cheese. It enjoyed itself. That's what worries me.

up.label: Seal the vault
up.reaction: Sealed. It's knocking. Politely, so far.

cards.text: The cheese has left the vault. It's in the library. It has taken out a book. The book is 'Leadership'.

right.label: Revoke its library card
right.reaction: It didn't need the card. It has absorbed the book. Physically.

left.label: Let it read
left.reaction: It's on chapter four, 'Winning Hearts'. It is winning hearts.

cards.text: The cheese is back. The buyer returned it with a note: 'It knows my name.' We keep the money. I checked.

right.label: Back in the vault
right.reaction: It went quietly. It left a small cheese behind. A scout.

left.label: Sell it again
left.reaction: Sold to Worse Town. They deserve each other.

cards.text: The cheese is polling at 12% for Sunday. It hasn't said a word. Voters are calling that 'refreshing'.

right.label: Debate the cheese
right.reaction: It said nothing for an hour. The Bugle called it 'statesmanlike'.

left.label: Offer it Doug's job
left.reaction: The cheese is Treasurer. The budget has never smelled stronger. Doug is its intern.

cards.text: I've filed the paperwork. The town now legally owns the moon. We just need a flag. And a very long pole.

right.label: Plant the flag
right.reaction: It's ours. Don't look at it without a permit.

left.label: Sell the moon to Chad
left.reaction: He renamed it 'Chad's Night Light'.

cards.text: The moon has replied. By post. It says it never agreed to be owned and is 'considering its options'. The tide is already odd.

right.label: Apologise to the moon
right.reaction: Accepted. The tide is back where it was. Mostly. The pond is still acting up.

left.label: We have the paperwork
left.reaction: The moon has stopped coming out on Tuesdays. In protest.

cards.text: Bad news. 'Chad's Night Light' costs a fortune. It's huge and it's on all night. Can the town pay my moon bill?

right.label: Pay the moon bill
right.reaction: The moon stays on. You're welcome, everybody. It was that or darkness.

left.label: Turn the moon off
left.reaction: He did. He actually did. It's very dark. People keep falling into Kevin.

cards.text: We've been twinned with a town called Worse Town. They're visiting today. They already look disappointed.

right.label: Throw a welcome party
right.reaction: They loved it. They've asked to be adopted.

left.label: Show them the pothole
left.reaction: Their mayor wept. 'It's bigger than ours,' he said.

cards.text: All of Worse Town has moved in. All 300 of them. They say it's 'so much less worse here'. They're living in the gym.

right.label: Welcome them properly
right.reaction: They cried. They'd never seen a second traffic light before.

left.label: Send them home
left.reaction: They left. Slowly. Looking back. One of them waved. You monster.

cards.text: Worse Town is empty now. I'd like to buy it. 'Chad Town.' We'd be twinned. I'd be mayor. You'd curtsy.

right.label: Sell him Worse Town
right.reaction: Chad Town opens Monday. Population: Chad. He's already unpopular there.

left.label: It isn't ours to sell
left.reaction: Technically correct. 'The worst kind of correct,' says Chad.

cards.text: The school has one textbook. It's about boats. We are four hundred miles from water.

right.label: Buy new books
right.reaction: The PTA approves. We've never said that before.

left.label: Buy a boat
left.reaction: The children can all tie knots now. They're thriving.

down.label: Boats are educational
down.reaction: The PTA has started a newsletter. About you.

cards.text: I'm giving the town a statue. Of me. Forty feet tall. It winks. At noon it says 'You're welcome' in my voice.

right.label: Accept the statue
right.reaction: It winks at night too. Pigeons won't land on it. It 'makes eye contact'.

left.label: No statues
left.reaction: Then I'll put it just outside town. Facing in. Winking.

cards.text: It's my birthday. Can the whole town have fireworks? I told the whole town yes. I'm eight. I'm in charge.

right.label: Fireworks for Timmy
right.reaction: BEST. MAYOR. EVER.

left.label: One sparkler
left.reaction: It's... one. It's a small one.

cards.text: I need a weather radar. Right now I lick my finger and hold it up. My finger is exhausted. It's seen things, Mayor.

right.label: Buy the radar
right.reaction: It works! I can see the rain coming. It's coming from above. I knew it.

left.label: The finger is fine
left.reaction: Tomorrow's forecast: finger. Sixty per cent chance of finger.

cards.text: A wizard has moved into the clock tower. Every hour, instead of chiming, it says 'Ooooh'. He pays rent in sparkles.

right.label: Evict the wizard
right.reaction: He left. The clock still says 'Ooooh'.

left.label: Make him town magician
left.reaction: He turned the bins into doves. The doves are bins now.

cards.text: The wizard has turned the police station into a frog. One big frog. We're inside it. It's quite roomy, actually.

right.label: Make him turn it back
right.reaction: It's a station again. It still ribbits when you shut the door.

left.label: Keep the frog station
left.reaction: Crime is down. Nobody wants to be put in the frog.

cards.text: The bus route has become a circle. It's gone round for a week. The passengers have formed a government.

right.label: Add a stop
right.reaction: They got off. Some of them got back on. They miss it.

left.label: Recognise their government
left.reaction: They've declared independence. Seat 14 is the capital.

cards.text: The Bus Republic has issued passports. You need one to board. I was refused entry. I am the police.

right.label: Apply for a visa
right.reaction: Approved. Your passport photo is a drawing by the driver. You're a potato.

left.label: Invade the bus
left.reaction: You got on. You couldn't get a seat. Humiliating. For everyone.

cards.text: The Bus Republic wants a trade deal. They offer gossip, a lost umbrella and a very warm seat. They want a second bus.

right.label: Sign the deal
right.reaction: Two buses. They've formed a parliament. It sits at every red light.

left.label: No deal
left.reaction: Sanctions. Nobody on the bus will make eye contact with you.

cards.text: The Bugle wants karaoke night at City Hall. You'd sing first. You'd sing 'the hard one'.

right.label: Sing the hard one
right.reaction: Your high note broke a window. Front page.

left.label: No singing in City Hall
left.reaction: The silence is deafening. Marge is writing about it.

cards.text: Someone painted a zebra crossing. With a real zebra. It won't move. Traffic has stopped. The zebra seems content.

right.label: Hire a zebra wrangler
right.reaction: Moved. It's on the roundabout now. Content.

left.label: Make it official
left.reaction: Everyone crosses by the zebra. It nods at them.

cards.text: Every traffic light went green at once. Nobody's crashed. Everyone is being polite. Nobody can leave.

right.label: Fix the lights
right.reaction: Red, amber, green. The town wept with relief.

left.label: Leave them green
left.reaction: Society has entered a politeness spiral. It's beautiful.

cards.text: Your official portrait is done. The artist painted you as a bear. A good bear. A dignified bear.

right.label: Hang it proudly
right.reaction: The bear looks over City Hall. People salute it.

left.label: Pay for a repaint
left.reaction: Now you're a smaller bear. Progress.

cards.text: The dog show needs a judge. All forty dogs are Sergeant Biscuit. Barb says that's 'not possible'.

right.label: Every dog wins
right.reaction: Forty rosettes. All Biscuit. He's unbearable now.

left.label: Find the real Biscuit
left.reaction: Found him. The other thirty-nine were raccoons.

cards.text: The town marathon is today. Nobody trained. The route goes through the bakery. Twice.

right.label: Run it yourself
right.reaction: You finished. You ate a pie. Nobody's counting.

left.label: Postpone it
left.reaction: Postponed. Three people are still running.

cards.text: I want to turn the old fire station into an arcade. The fire engine is a ride now. It still has water in it.

right.label: Open the arcade
right.reaction: First ride soaked the deputy mayor. Fun for all.

left.label: Firefighters only
left.reaction: The firefighters have the high score. Of course.

cards.text: I'd like to pave the park. For parking. Think of it as a very flat park. With cars for trees.

right.label: Pave the park
right.reaction: The ducks are circling, looking for the pond. It's bay 14 now.

left.label: Hands off the park
left.reaction: Trees don't shop, you know. I've checked. Not one loyalty card.

cards.text: The Bugle is staging an opera about you. Four hours. You die in act one. The rest is the funeral.

right.label: Attend and applaud
right.reaction: You cried at your own funeral. That's tomorrow's photo.

left.label: Ban the opera
left.reaction: Banned. So now it's a musical. A longer one.

cards.text: A heatwave is coming. Or a cold snap. It's definitely one of those. Either way, the public pool has a crack in it.

right.label: Fix the pool
right.reaction: It snowed. The pool looks great. Bev is ice skating on it. Backwards.

left.label: Tell people to drink water
left.reaction: Hot, with a chance of angry. Someone fried an egg on Kevin.

cards.text: I gave some squirrels a loan. I was very tired. They put up acorns as collateral. They've defaulted.

right.label: Repossess the acorns
right.reaction: We own nine hundred acorns. The squirrels are watching.

left.label: Forgive the loan
left.reaction: They chittered. One saluted.

cards.text: The squirrels have opened a bank. Opposite ours. Better interest. They pay in acorns. People are switching.

right.label: Compete on rates
right.reaction: We pay in acorns now too. Nobody knows what anything's worth. The economy is nuts.

left.label: Shut the squirrel bank
left.reaction: Closed. They operate out of a tree now. You can't regulate a tree.

cards.text: There's a monster in the reservoir. It's very shy. I only know because it returned my umbrella.

right.label: Put it on the brochure
right.reaction: Tourists everywhere. The monster sent a note: 'please stop'.

left.label: Protect its privacy
left.reaction: It left a fish on your doorstep. You're friends now.

cards.text: Someone stole the 'Welcome' sign. And the backup sign. And my backup badge. Morale is very low.

right.label: Pay for overtime
right.reaction: We'll find the sign. Or a similar sign.

left.label: Blame the next town over
left.reaction: Classic them.

cards.text: There are people outside City Hall with signs. Some of the signs are about you. All of the signs, actually.

right.label: Go out and listen
right.reaction: They yelled. You nodded. Everyone feels slightly better.

left.label: Lock the doors
left.reaction: They're singing now. Badly. On purpose.

cards.text: Business is so bad I've had to sell my third yacht. My second yacht is lonely. Do something.

right.label: Cut business rates
right.reaction: My yachts thank you. Both of them.

left.label: Get a smaller yacht
left.reaction: 'Mayor Mocks Yacht Owner.' I'll be in the papers.

cards.text: The Bugle has a story about you. It's not true. It doesn't need to be. It's in a very big font.

right.label: Give Marge an interview
right.reaction: Lovely. I'll quote you creatively.

left.label: Ignore it
left.reaction: The font got bigger.

cards.text: We are nearly out of money. I've started counting the coins in the fountain. It's mostly buttons.

right.label: Sell the spoon statue
right.reaction: Sold. The town feels emptier. Spoonless.

left.label: Tax hats
left.reaction: Very tall hats pay double.

cards.text: The people love you so much they'd like free ice cream. Every day. They said you'd say yes.

right.label: Free ice cream
right.reaction: They want sprinkles next.

left.label: Say no nicely
left.reaction: They took it badly. One man lay down.

cards.text: Business is so good I'd like to buy the town. Not all of it. Just the parts with roads.

right.label: Sell him Main Street
right.reaction: Welcome to Chad Street. Tolls start Monday.

left.label: Refuse
left.reaction: Everything has a price. I'll wait.

cards.text: With this much support I've started arresting people for jaywalking. And for walking. Thoughts?

right.label: Rein her in
right.reaction: Fine. Walking is legal again.

left.label: Let it ride
left.reaction: The streets have never been emptier.

cards.text: We love you so much we went through your bins. You eat a LOT of string cheese. It's tomorrow's front page.

right.label: Own it
right.reaction: 'Mayor: I Regret Nothing.' Perfect.

left.label: Bury the story
left.reaction: What story? Exactly.

cards.text: Your treasury is bursting. Lend me some? I'll pay it back. With interest. Probably. Possibly.

right.label: Lend it to Chad
right.reaction: A pleasure. I'll send a postcard from the yacht.

left.label: Spend it on the town
left.reaction: A new bench! On every corner! Too many benches!

cards.text: A rival billionaire moved to town. His hat is taller than mine. I need a law about hats. Today. Before lunch.

right.label: Ban tall hats
right.reaction: Justice. Barb is out measuring hats. She's arrested a chef.

left.label: Hats are free
left.reaction: He's put a second hat on the first hat. I'm ordering a third. This ends in the clouds.

cards.text: The library wants to open at night. The best books only talk after dark. The cookbooks get very honest.

right.label: Fund night opening
right.reaction: Shh. They're starting. The atlas is telling everyone where it's been.

left.label: Libraries close at five
left.reaction: That's what the daytime books want you to think. Cowards.

cards.text: The fountain is full of coins. People make wishes. Legally those are our coins. Emotionally, less so.

right.label: Collect the coins
right.reaction: £41.12 and a button. Nobody's wishes are coming true now. Including mine.

left.label: Leave the wishes
left.reaction: Someone wished for a pony. There's a pony now. Who's paying for the pony?

cards.text: The town choir only knows one song. It's the bin schedule, set to music. They'd like a second song.

right.label: Fund music lessons
right.reaction: They know two songs now. Both are about bins.

left.label: One song is plenty
left.reaction: They sang it at you. For an hour.

cards.text: Chad's delivery drones keep dropping parcels on the police station. I've received forty hats.

right.label: Ban the drones
right.reaction: The hats stopped. I'm keeping the hats.

left.label: Charge Chad rent for the sky
left.reaction: The sky is a revenue stream now.

cards.text: Someone is stealing pies from windowsills. The crumbs lead to the police station.

right.label: Investigate Barb
right.reaction: Barb confessed. To 'a few'. It was eleven.

left.label: Pie locks for everyone
left.reaction: The thief now steals locks.

cards.text: The only snowplow is broken. School road or Chad's shopping street? The other stays buried.

right.label: Plow the school road
right.reaction: The shops are an igloo now.

left.label: Plow Chad Street
left.reaction: The school is an igloo now.

up.label: Rent a second plow
up.reaction: Two plows. I need to sit down.

cards.text: I want a billboard on City Hall. My face. Forty feet. The words 'TRUST CHAD'. The eyes follow you. That's a feature.

right.label: Allow it
right.reaction: It lights up at night. Nobody within two miles has slept. But they trust me.

left.label: No billboard
left.reaction: Then where do people look when they need to trust me? Think about that.

cards.text: Gerald has volunteered to be the school crossing guard. He's already bought the hat. It's a tiny hat.

right.label: Give him the job
right.reaction: Traffic has stopped. All of it. For hours.

left.label: Hire a human
left.reaction: Honk. (He is wearing the hat anyway.)

cards.text: Someone has donated a bench. It's dedicated to 'The Mayor, Who We Tolerate'. It's very comfortable.

right.label: Keep the bench
right.reaction: It's become a tourist spot. People sit and tolerate.

left.label: Change the plaque
left.reaction: It now says 'The Mayor'. Somehow that's worse.

cards.text: The PTA talent show needs a judge. Forty children. One song. It's the same song. It's about you.

right.label: Judge honestly
right.reaction: 'Mayor Makes Children Cry.' Front page.

left.label: Everyone wins
left.reaction: Forty trophies. You're paying for forty trophies.

cards.text: A rival paper has started: The Whistle. First headline: 'BUGLE EDITOR SMELLS'. I want it shut down. For journalism.

right.label: Shut it down
right.reaction: One paper. One voice. Tomorrow's headline: 'BUGLE EDITOR SMELLS GREAT'.

left.label: A free press is good
left.reaction: Is it? Today's Whistle: 'MAYOR'S HAIR: AN INVESTIGATION'. Eleven pages.

cards.text: Chad's hand is creeping toward the treasury jar. He keeps glancing at you. Slap it away when he's not looking.

right.label: Slap!
right.reaction: OW. I was 'checking it was still there'.

left.label: He saw you coming
left.reaction: Ah ah ah. Finders keepers. Treasurers weepers.

cards.text: Gerald is stealing the bread from the council lunch. One loaf at a time. Grab it back when he's not looking.

right.label: Got it!
right.reaction: HONK. (A grudging respect.)

left.label: He saw you
left.reaction: He honked at you so hard your hair moved.

cards.text: Randy is 'reorganising' the evidence room into his coat. Snatch the evidence back while his back is turned.

right.label: Snatched it
right.reaction: Boss! I was... dusting it. With my mouth.

left.label: Caught in the act
left.reaction: We saw you. All three of us saw you.

cards.text: Marge is photographing the papers on your desk for tomorrow's front page. Turn them over when she's not looking.

right.label: Turned over
right.reaction: Clever. I'll just print the back of the paper then.

left.label: Flash!
left.reaction: 'MAYOR'S SHOPPING LIST: TWELVE CHEESES.' Lovely.

cards.text: Barb is about to give your car a parking ticket. Move it before she looks up from her notepad.

right.label: Moved it
right.reaction: Where did your car go. Where did your car GO.

left.label: Ticketed
left.reaction: That's a fine. And a fine for the fine.

cards.text: Timmy has drawn a moustache on your official portrait. Wipe it off before the press arrives. He's guarding it.

right.label: Wiped clean
right.reaction: Noooo. It was a good moustache.

left.label: Too late
left.reaction: The moustache made the front page. People like it more.

cards.text: Someone ordered forty tonnes of confetti on the town account. For 'morale'. It arrived. It's in the bank.

right.label: Throw a parade
right.reaction: Morale is up. The bank is a snow globe.

left.label: Send it back
left.reaction: The return fee is also forty tonnes. Of confetti.

cards.text: Bees have moved into City Hall's photocopier. Every copy comes out slightly sticky and humming.

right.label: Keep the bees
right.reaction: Minutes now come with honey. Attendance is up.

left.label: Call a beekeeper
left.reaction: The beekeeper is also humming. Suspicious.

cards.text: I've installed a vending machine in your office. It only sells my autobiography. It's forty pounds.

right.label: Leave it
right.reaction: Three sold. All to me. To keep the numbers up.

left.label: Unplug it
left.reaction: It's still reading itself aloud. In my voice.

cards.text: The town clock has been seven minutes fast for thirty years. Fixing it means everyone is late, permanently.

right.label: Fix the clock
right.reaction: Everyone arrived seven minutes late. Furious, together.

left.label: Keep it fast
left.reaction: Tradition is just a clock that's wrong on purpose.

cards.text: A seagull has stolen the weather report. Mid-broadcast. It's on the roof with it. It looks confident.

right.label: Let the seagull forecast
right.reaction: 'Chips. Later chips.' Accurate, actually.

left.label: Negotiate with chips
left.reaction: It took the chips and the report. Classic gull.

cards.text: The seagull has my job now. And my desk. And my lunch. Its forecasts are 100% right. Mine were 'vibes'. I'd like to appeal.

right.label: Give Steve his job back
right.reaction: The gull took it well. It took Steve's sandwich better.

left.label: The gull stays
left.reaction: 'Chips. Then light chips.' Steve is its assistant now. He holds the chips.

cards.text: Somebody returned a library book that went out in 1952. With a note: 'Sorry. It was a long book.'

right.label: Waive the fine
right.reaction: The fine was nine thousand pounds. It's gone now. Like 1952.

left.label: Charge the fine
left.reaction: They paid. In 1952 money. It's mostly buttons.

cards.text: My new robot can do your job. It's cheaper. It's never late. It does say 'EXTERMINATE' sometimes.

right.label: Give it a trial
right.reaction: It approved three bridges and a moat. Nobody asked for a moat.

left.label: Unplug the robot
left.reaction: It's sulking in the cupboard. Robots can sulk now.

cards.text: The robot did the budget in four seconds. It's perfect. Now it's crying. I know that cry. That's my cry.

right.label: Comfort the robot
right.reaction: It hugged Doug. Doug hugged it. They share a desk now. And a tissue box.

left.label: Return it to Chad
left.reaction: Chad says no refunds for 'emotional damage to merchandise'.

cards.text: My robot has joined the Goose Union. It honks now. I want it back. It says it has found 'its people'.

right.label: Side with the robot
right.reaction: HONK. EXTERMINATE. HONK. (It's happy.)

left.label: Side with Chad
left.reaction: Returned. It honks in sleep mode. Chad can't turn that off.

cards.text: The geese would like a postbox. For goose letters. They're mostly complaints. About you.

right.label: Install it
right.reaction: The first letter just says 'HONK'. It's underlined.

left.label: No goose post
left.reaction: They're posting complaints through your cat flap now.

cards.text: Two people want you to marry them. In the fountain. At midnight. They're both called Kevin.

right.label: Officiate
right.reaction: Lovely ceremony. Kevin the pothole sent flowers.

left.label: Politely decline
left.reaction: They got married by a goose instead. Legally binding, apparently.

cards.text: I'd like to sell hot dogs at the war memorial. Tasteful hot dogs. With a little flag.

right.label: Absolutely not
right.reaction: Fine. I'll sell flags with a little hot dog.

left.label: One tasteful stand
left.reaction: Business is great. Grandparents are livid.

cards.text: A busker has played the same three notes outside the school for eleven days. The children now hum it in their sleep.

right.label: Buy him more notes
right.reaction: Four notes now. It's a whole different song.

left.label: Move him on
left.reaction: He's playing the three notes outside your house.

cards.text: Readers want to know why the mayor has no official hat. The last mayor had a hat. It had a goose on it.

right.label: Commission a hat
right.reaction: It's tall. It's purple. It has a small bell.

left.label: Hats are vanity
left.reaction: 'MAYOR HATLESS, HEARTLESS.' Today's front page.

cards.text: A dog walked into the station and handed itself in. It won't say what it did. It's been here three days.

right.label: Set it free
right.reaction: It left. It came back. It's confessing to something new.

left.label: Investigate the dog
left.reaction: It was the pie thief. Case closed. Pies returned.

cards.text: A swan has asked to join the Goose Union. The geese are divided. It's a very fancy swan.

right.label: Back the swan
right.reaction: Integration! The swan is now treasurer. It's very good.

left.label: Geese only
left.reaction: The swan has started a rival union. It's posher.

cards.text: Good news, there's a hole in the budget. Bad news, it's an actual hole. In the budget office.

right.label: Fill it
right.reaction: Filled. With the budget. That was the budget.

left.label: Use it as a filing system
left.reaction: Very efficient. Nobody can find anything.

cards.text: The PTA's compost heap has become sentient. It's very polite. It would like a seat on the council.

right.label: Give it a seat
right.reaction: It sits quietly. Smells strongly. Votes sensibly.

left.label: Turn it over
left.reaction: It's taken it personally. Rot is coming.

cards.text: Councillor Compost has tabled its first motion: 'More rot.' It passed. Nobody likes to vote against a heap.

right.label: Veto the rot
right.reaction: Vetoed. The heap has gone very quiet. Warm, and very quiet.

left.label: Let the rot commence
left.reaction: The allotments have never been greener. The high street has never smelled worse.

cards.text: I've dug a moat round my house. Now my house is an island. Can it be its own town? Tax-wise?

right.label: Grant independence
right.reaction: Chadland has a flag. It is his face.

left.label: Fill in the moat
left.reaction: Fine. I'll dig a bigger one.

cards.text: An anonymous artist built a sculpture in the square. It's a giant ear. Linda says it is 'listening'.

right.label: Keep the ear
right.reaction: It's popular. People whisper secrets into it. Linda takes notes.

left.label: Remove the ear
left.reaction: It's gone. There's a giant mouth there now.

cards.text: My train set is now so big it's in the town hall. And the bank. Can it be the town's train set?

right.label: Official town railway
right.reaction: All aboard! It goes round the bank. Twice.

left.label: Pack it away
left.reaction: I'm going on strike. The trains are going on strike.

cards.text: I predicted sun. It snowed. Indoors. I'd like to retire, or be promoted. Either feels right.

right.label: Promote Steve
right.reaction: Chief Forecaster. Bigger hat. The hat is also wrong about the weather.

left.label: Let him retire
left.reaction: He's retired to the roof. Still forecasting. Louder. For free.

cards.text: The school egg-and-spoon race has been banned for 'speed'. Parents are livid. One parent is a goose.

right.label: Unban it
right.reaction: The goose won. Gerald is unbearable.

left.label: Safety first
left.reaction: The PTA is now staging a spoon-only race. In protest.

cards.text: Your speech yesterday was translated into sign language by a mime. It's gone viral. Nobody knows what you said.

right.label: Make him official
right.reaction: Every speech is now silent. Approval is up.

left.label: Issue a correction
left.reaction: The correction was also mimed. It's worse.

cards.text: The new town coins have your face on them. The face is upside down. People are flipping them to check.

right.label: Reprint them
right.reaction: Now you're the right way up. And slightly cross-eyed.

left.label: Collector's edition
left.reaction: Sold out. Nobody spends them. You're on every mantelpiece upside down.

cards.text: If I can't have a helicopter, can I have a helipad? For morale. I'll stand on it. Hopefully.

right.label: Build a helipad
right.reaction: I stood on it for six hours. Nothing came. Best day of my life.

left.label: No
left.reaction: I've painted an H on my driveway. It's the same.

cards.text: The charity duck race was won by a real duck. It wasn't entered. It wants the prize money.

right.label: Pay the duck
right.reaction: The duck donated it to the geese. Politics.

left.label: Disqualify the duck
left.reaction: The duck has a lawyer. It's another duck.

cards.text: We need a town song. Readers submitted one. It's mostly about Kevin. The pothole. It's very moving.

right.label: Adopt the Kevin song
right.reaction: The town anthem is about a hole. People weep at sports events.

left.label: Write a new one
left.reaction: The new one is about you. Nobody can sing it.

cards.text: The fog is so thick that two people got married without meeting. They seem happy. Should we clear it?

right.label: Buy fog fans
right.reaction: Clear skies! The couple are disappointed by each other.

left.label: Leave the fog
left.reaction: Crime is up. So are weddings.

cards.text: The library has an overdue book. It's checked out to you. It's called 'How To Be A Good Mayor'.

right.label: Return it unread
right.reaction: Classic. The book's sighing.

left.label: Renew it again
left.reaction: Ninth renewal. The book has given up on you.

cards.text: The raccoons would like a PR campaign. 'Bins Are For Everyone'. They've made a poster. It's mostly smudges.

right.label: Fund the campaign
right.reaction: Bins Are For Everyone. Bins are now for everyone.

left.label: Bins are for rubbish
left.reaction: Agreed. And we... the raccoons... are not rubbish.

cards.text: Play me at chess. If you win, I'll leave town. If I win, I get the bell tower. I've already measured it.

right.label: Play him
right.reaction: You lost in four moves. He's ringing the bell. On the hour.

left.label: Decline
left.reaction: Coward's move. Bishop to bell tower.

cards.text: I sneezed at the craft fair and now the whole town is glittery. It won't come off. Ever.

right.label: Embrace the sparkle
right.reaction: The town shimmers. Criminals are very easy to spot.

left.label: Hire cleaners
left.reaction: They're glittery now too. It spreads.

cards.text: The glitter has reached the reservoir. The water sparkles. So do the people who drink it. From the inside. I can see Doug's lunch.

right.label: Emergency de-glittering
right.reaction: Clean. Mostly. Doug still glows a bit when he's nervous. So, always.

left.label: Sell it as fancy water
left.reaction: 'Bad Town Sparkling.' It's selling. Customers light up. Literally.

cards.text: I'd like to open a museum of things the town has lost. It's mostly umbrellas and one mayor.

right.label: Open the museum
right.reaction: The lost mayor is the main exhibit. He waves.

left.label: No museum
left.reaction: The umbrellas have been returned. To nobody.

cards.text: I bought every left shoe in town. You'll need to buy them back. For a reasonable price. Per shoe.

right.label: Buy them back
right.reaction: Thank you. Now about the right shoes...

left.label: Hopping is free
left.reaction: The town is hopping. Productivity is down. Calves are up.

cards.text: The scarecrow at the allotments has been elected allotment chair. Unopposed. Nobody else turned up.

right.label: Recognise the scarecrow
right.reaction: Its first act: more crows. Bold.

left.label: Overturn the result
left.reaction: It's appealing. Its hand is a rake.

cards.text: The scarecrow runs the allotments better than anyone ever has. The carrots are enormous. People ask why you can't be more like it.

right.label: Take lessons from it
right.reaction: You stood in a field all day saying nothing. Approval went up four points.

left.label: Fire the scarecrow
left.reaction: It didn't react. Somehow it still won the argument.

cards.text: The geese are holding a family reunion. Four thousand geese. In the park. For a week. Bring snacks.

right.label: Supply snacks
right.reaction: They're grateful. They're everywhere. Grateful everywhere.

left.label: Close the park
left.reaction: They reunited in the bank instead.

cards.text: The bake sale made a cake shaped like you. It's very accurate. Someone has already eaten your left ear.

right.label: Auction the cake
right.reaction: Chad bought it. He's eating it at you.

left.label: Eat it yourself
left.reaction: 'MAYOR EATS SELF.' Front page, obviously.

cards.text: The Bugle's new antenna picks up a radio station from 1974. It's just a man reading out bin schedules. Ratings are huge.

right.label: Make it official
right.reaction: The man is now our most popular presenter. He doesn't know.

left.label: Retune it
left.reaction: You've found a new station. It's Randy. Talking to bins.

cards.text: Council staff want nap pods. I said no. They've built them out of filing cabinets. They look very comfortable.

right.label: Allow naps
right.reaction: Productivity down. Happiness extremely up.

left.label: Ban the pods
left.reaction: They sleep standing up now. Like horses.

cards.text: The frogs have learned a song. It's the town song. Badly. Every night. All night.

right.label: Book them for the festival
right.reaction: Standing ovation. Mostly from other frogs.

left.label: Earplugs for all
left.reaction: Earplugs bought. The frogs have learned to sing louder.

cards.text: My yacht is stuck in the fountain. Don't ask how. Can we drain the fountain? Or widen the town?

right.label: Drain the fountain
right.reaction: The yacht is free. The wishes are lost. Mine came true.

left.label: It lives there now
left.reaction: Tourists love the fountain yacht. Chad is furious.

cards.text: Mrs. Higgins is 104 and wants to arm-wrestle the mayor for the key to the town. She's trained for this.

right.label: Accept the challenge
right.reaction: You lost. Instantly. She has the key. She's using it.

left.label: Give her the key
left.reaction: She's opened every door in town. Every single one.

cards.text: Mrs Higgins, 104, has used the key to the town to open the bank, the jail and the zoo. We didn't have a zoo. We do now.

right.label: Ask for the key back
right.reaction: She arm-wrestled Barb for it. Barb's arm is in a sling. Barb is impressed.

left.label: Make her Head of Doors
left.reaction: Every door in town is open. Forever. Draughty, but friendly.

cards.text: Can we have a skate park? I've got a skateboard. I can't skate. I'd like to fall off somewhere official.

right.label: Build a skate park
right.reaction: Timmy fell off at once. Bev did a kickflip over him. She's ninety-seven.

left.label: Skate at home
left.reaction: I'm skating in the town hall now. Down the stairs. Doug is a ramp.

cards.text: A man with a very long beard is blocking the high street. Not on purpose. It's just very long.

right.label: Trim the beard
right.reaction: He's devastated. The beard had a name.

left.label: Make it a landmark
left.reaction: People take photos with the beard. It's a tourist hotspot.

cards.text: Someone is digging a tunnel under the bank. I'm not saying it's me. But I've got a lot of soil on my shoes.

right.label: Investigate the tunnel
right.reaction: It leads to the cheese vault. Of course it does.

left.label: Pretend you didn't hear
left.reaction: The bank is lighter today. Weirdly lighter.

cards.text: A street lamp has been flickering in Morse code for a week. Linda decoded it. It says 'LOWER MY TAXES'.

right.label: Lower the lamp's taxes
right.reaction: It's glowing steadily now. Smugly.

left.label: Replace the lamp
left.reaction: The new lamp is also flickering. 'WE REMEMBER.'

cards.text: The town's statue of the founder has gone missing. It was last seen walking towards the coast.

right.label: Search the coast
right.reaction: Found it. It was watching the sea. It seemed at peace.

left.label: Build a new founder
left.reaction: The new founder looks like Chad. Chad paid for it.

cards.text: Boss. The raccoons have entered the talent show. Their act is 'eating a bin'. They're very good at it.

right.label: Let them compete
right.reaction: They won. They ate the trophy.

left.label: Ban the raccoons
left.reaction: They've entered again. In a trench coat. As Randy.

cards.text: Boss. Small thing. When I stepped down, I kept the keys to City Hall. Sentimental reasons. Not giving them back.

right.label: Ask nicely for the keys
right.reaction: Asking nicely. Classic rookie. The keys are somewhere safe. My mouth.

left.label: Change the locks
left.reaction: Lovely new locks. I've got copies already. I was at the locksmith's first.

up.label: Make him Keeper of Keys
up.reaction: A title! Mum will be so proud. Mum is also a raccoon.

cards.text: Your deputy is holding 'shadow council meetings' in the bins behind City Hall. Attendance is excellent. It's all raccoons.

right.label: Attend a meeting
right.reaction: They voted you Bin Treasurer. You already owe them eleven crisps.

left.label: Ban bin meetings
left.reaction: They moved to the recycling. Technically a different building.

cards.text: The new locks are great, boss. Really strong. So I've moved City Hall. It's in my coat now. Most of it.

right.label: Demand City Hall back
right.reaction: Fine! But I'm keeping the good stapler. And the bit with the clock.

left.label: Work from the coat
left.reaction: Cosy. Bit dark. Something in the left pocket bit Doug.

cards.text: Randy has made your campaign posters without asking. They say 'VOTE {mayor}: NOT A RACCOON'. He's very proud.

right.label: Put them up
right.reaction: Now everyone suspects you might be a raccoon. Randy calls this 'buzz'.

left.label: Take them down
left.reaction: He's made new ones. 'VOTE {mayor}: PROBABLY NOT A RACCOON'.

cards.text: Boss! I've organised you a campaign rally. Venue: the bins. Crowd: 300. Raccoons: 290. Will you do a speech?

right.label: Give the speech
right.reaction: They hissed for twenty minutes. In raccoon, that's a standing ovation.

left.label: Cancel the rally
left.reaction: Randy went on alone. Said lovely things about you for an hour. Then ate the podium.

cards.text: I'm ninety-seven and I want the speed limit raised on Elm Street. My scooter does forty. I had it looked at. By me.

right.label: Raise the limit
right.reaction: WHEEEEE. (She is already past the post office.)

left.label: Absolutely not
left.reaction: I've outlived four mayors, dear. I can wait you out.

cards.text: Bev just did Elm Street in eleven seconds. Wheelie at the end. She's challenging my police car to a race.

right.label: Let them race
right.reaction: Bev won. She lapped the car. She stopped for a scone halfway.

left.label: Impound the scooter
left.reaction: She's walking now. She walks faster than the scooter. It's worse.

cards.text: I've got a petition to raise the speed limit. 400 signatures. All mine. I've got wonderful stamina for signing.

right.label: Accept the petition
right.reaction: Lovely. See you at the finish line, dear.

left.label: One person, one signature
left.reaction: Fine. I'll get my sisters. They're ninety-nine. They're quicker.

cards.text: Bev wants a proper race. The Bad Town Grand Prix. Mobility scooters only. Twelve entries. Nine of them are Bev.

right.label: Host the Grand Prix
right.reaction: Bev came first, second and sixth. She's banned from podiums now.

left.label: Health and safety says no
left.reaction: Bev called you a 'wet lettuce'. It's on a T-shirt. Bev is selling them.

cards.text: My client, Mr Whiskers (me), is suing the town. There was a sunbeam on the library floor yesterday. It is gone.

right.label: Settle out of court
right.reaction: My client accepts. In tuna. Unopened. His paws are delicate.

left.label: See you in court
left.reaction: Excellent. I'll be the one in the box. The cardboard one.

cards.text: Court is in session. The judge is my client. The jury is a box my client is sitting in. How do you plead?

right.label: Not guilty
right.reaction: Overruled. Guilty. Sentence: one hour of stroking my client.

left.label: Knock his gavel off the desk
left.reaction: He did not see that coming. He knocked yours off. It's escalating.

cards.text: Mr Whiskers has now sued the library, the bakery and Tuesday. He won all three. Tuesday owes him tuna.

right.label: Hire him instead
right.reaction: He's Town Solicitor. He billed us for a four-hour nap. 'Research'.

left.label: Ban cat lawsuits
left.reaction: He's challenging the ban. In court. His court.

cards.text: New ruling: every box in Bad Town now belongs to my client. That includes the post office. And your car.

right.label: Appeal
right.reaction: Appeal denied. Appeal sat on. Appeal is warm now. Appeal is his.

left.label: Give him the boxes
left.reaction: My client is asleep in the post office. No post until he wakes.

cards.text: Big pitch. What if Bad Town was an app? Same town. Monthly fee. Dark mode. Dark mode is just night.

right.label: Launch the app
right.reaction: 'Bad Town+' is live. 3 downloads: me, Randy and an accident.

left.label: The town is free
left.reaction: That's exactly what someone with no vision says. Going on the podcast.

up.label: Do a podcast instead
up.reaction: Episode one is nine hours. Six of them are me saying 'right'.

cards.text: Update: Bad Town+ has ads now. On the fountain. Every splash says 'brought to you by Chad'.

right.label: Keep the ads
right.reaction: The fountain sounds tired. It says 'brought to you by' in its sleep.

left.label: Pull the ads
left.reaction: Unsubscribing a fountain is a premium feature. But fine.

cards.text: Brayden's podcast is the most listened-to in Bad Town. He plays it from the clock tower. At 5 am.

right.label: Unplug the speaker
right.reaction: He's recorded an episode about being unplugged. It's slightly quieter.

left.label: Give him noon
left.reaction: Noon is 'Brayden Hour' now. It's four hours long.

cards.text: Brayden asked me to make his app 'smarter'. Done. It now runs the town better than you. It wants your office.

right.label: Unplug it
right.reaction: It sent you a very polite email about this. It cc'd the Bugle.

left.label: Give it the office
left.reaction: It works all night. It has fired Doug twice. Doug still comes in.

cards.text: Good news: I built a weather machine. Bad news: the only setting is 'soup'. Tomorrow is minestrone.

right.label: Fund more research
right.reaction: Three settings now! Soup, gravy and 'surprise'. Nobody likes surprise.

left.label: Switch it off
left.reaction: It won't switch off. It's sulking. Light drizzle of broth.

up.label: Free lunch for all
up.reaction: Lunch falls from the sky. Everyone carries a bowl now. Spoons sold out.

cards.text: Weather update: it is raining gravy. I'll be honest, I don't know how to present this. I just said 'beefy'.

right.label: Sell it to the bakery
right.reaction: Gravy pies. Gravy bread. Gravy gravy. Everyone's sticky. Business booms.

left.label: Shelter everyone
left.reaction: Everyone's in the gym. It smells incredible. People are dipping things.

cards.text: Tiny problem. The weather machine has fallen in love with the clock tower. It only rains on the clock tower now.

right.label: Let love bloom
right.reaction: The clock wears a tiny umbrella. Marge calls it the wedding of the year.

left.label: Separate them
left.reaction: It's raining tears now. Actual tears. Very salty. Great on chips.

cards.text: Mayor! The health inspector is coming. Please tell him the tyre in the soup is 'a crouton'. A big one.

right.label: It's a crouton
right.reaction: He had seconds. He's been chewing for three hours. Five stars.

left.label: Tell the truth
left.reaction: Closed for a week. The tyre has been rehomed. It went quietly.

cards.text: A guidebook gave me two stars! One for the food. One for the wheel alignment. Can I have a gala dinner?

right.label: Throw the gala
right.reaction: Black tie and black tyres. The soup was 'rubbery but elegant'.

left.label: Bit much
left.reaction: Fine. One star on the sign. The other star I keep in my heart. And my boot.

cards.text: Mayor! Town Olympics! Events: competitive queueing, synchronised complaining and the 100 metre walk to the bins.

right.label: Light the torch
right.reaction: Bev won the 100m. Randy won the bins. The queue is still going.

left.label: No Olympics
left.reaction: A queue has started anyway. Nobody knows what for. It's very long.

cards.text: Medal problem. Randy won every bin event. Now he wants a national anthem. He's written one. It's just a hiss.

right.label: Play the hiss
right.reaction: Everyone stood. Some wept. It was, honestly, quite moving.

left.label: Disqualify Randy
left.reaction: He's appealing. To Mr Whiskers. That's going to go badly for you.

cards.text: I've had a vision, Mayor {mayor}. On Thursday a great darkness falls over Bad Town. I'm never wrong.

right.label: Prepare the town
right.reaction: Thursday was sunny. The great darkness was Randy in a big coat.

left.label: Ignore her
left.reaction: When the darkness comes, don't come crying to me. It won't. But don't.

cards.text: New vision. Much clearer. A tall stranger will bring you money. A short stranger will take it. Then a goose.

right.label: Hire her as an advisor
right.reaction: She told you to wear purple. You did. Nothing happened. 'A sign.'

left.label: Ask for a refund
left.reaction: She saw that coming, she says. She didn't. She's furious.

cards.text: Marcel the mime has built an invisible wall around City Hall. Staff keep walking into it. Doug's nose is very sore.

right.label: Ask him to take it down
right.reaction: He mimed taking it down. Then mimed a door. You mime-knock now.

left.label: Arrest him
left.reaction: He mimed being dragged away. Very moving. Barb clapped.

cards.text: The invisible door is now the only way into City Hall. Staff mime their keys. Doug lost his. He's locked out.

right.label: Mime Doug a key
right.reaction: You mimed it perfectly. Marcel wept. Silently, obviously.

left.label: Walk straight through
left.reaction: You walked through. Marcel mimed devastation. Then he mimed a lawyer.

cards.text: I'd like the council to pay for my first tattoo. I'm ninety-seven. A skull. Holding a smaller skull. Holding a scone.

right.label: Fund the art
right.reaction: Gorgeous. The scone has a tiny skull on it too. Detail.

left.label: Not with public money
left.reaction: I'll pay myself. In coins from 1951. They're worth more now.

cards.text: I've a date with Randy tonight, dear. Very charming. Bit bitey. Can the council pay for dinner?

right.label: Pay for dinner
right.reaction: They went to Sal's. Randy ate a tyre. Bev ate the bill. True love.

left.label: No public money for dates
left.reaction: Fine. We'll eat in the bins. Randy says they're lovely this time of year.

cards.text: Boss. The office fridge. Someone ate everyone's lunch. It wasn't me. I want to be clear. Some of it was me.

right.label: Hold an inquiry
right.reaction: The inquiry found Randy guilty. Randy ate the inquiry.

left.label: Buy everyone lunch
left.reaction: Delicious. Randy had seconds. Randy also ate the receipt.

cards.text: Quick one, boss. If anyone asks, there's nothing in my coat. It's just a thick coat. (The coat sneezes.)

right.label: Search the coat
right.reaction: Three raccoons, a toaster, the Welcome sign and a fourth raccoon.

left.label: Bless you, coat
left.reaction: Thank you. The coat says thank you. I say thank you. Not the coat.

cards.text: Can I give the speech at school assembly? I've prepared. It's called 'Bins: A Love Story'. Mostly hissing.

right.label: Let him speak
right.reaction: Standing ovation. Three kids now want coats with raccoons in them.

left.label: Absolutely not
left.reaction: I'll do it anyway. From inside the school bins. Better acoustics.

cards.text: Honest question, boss. If I ate some ballots on Sunday, to help you, would that be bad? Very hypothetically.

right.label: Yes. Very bad.
right.reaction: Right. Right. Just checking. Please ignore the wrapper.

left.label: Hire a ballot guard
left.reaction: You hired a goose. The goose ate the ballots. Randy is furious. That was his idea.

cards.text: Someone has built a statue of you, Mayor {mayor}. Out of bin bags. Randy calls it 'a tribute'. It smells like one.

right.label: Unveil it
right.reaction: It was unveiled. Then eaten. By raccoons. A short tribute.

left.label: Take it down
left.reaction: Randy wept tiny raccoon tears. He's building another one. Bigger.

cards.text: Let's rebrand. New name: BADTWN. No vowels. Vowels are so last quarter. The logo is a goose in sunglasses.

right.label: Rebrand
right.reaction: The signs say BADTWN now. Bev can't say it. Bev calls it 'that'.

left.label: Bad Town stays
left.reaction: Fine. But I'm keeping the goose in sunglasses. It's Gerald. He loves it.

cards.text: I've turned my office into a 'creativity space'. It's a ball pit. Doug fell in on Tuesday. He hasn't come out.

right.label: Rescue Doug
right.reaction: Doug's out. He found nine coins and a lost intern. Morale is great.

left.label: He looks happy
left.reaction: Doug approves budgets from the ball pit now. He approves everything.

cards.text: I invented a dog translator. Every dog in Bad Town has been saying the same thing for years. It's 'post man'.

right.label: Fund the translator
right.reaction: We added cats. The cats said things I won't repeat. Mr Whiskers sued.

left.label: Some things are best unknown
left.reaction: Agreed. Although Biscuit just said something about you. Not nice.

cards.text: Small lab accident. There are now two Dougs. Both are worried. One is mainly worried about the other one.

right.label: Keep both Dougs
right.reaction: Double the budget checks. Double the crying. Weirdly productive.

left.label: Undo it
left.reaction: Undone. One Doug left. He's not sure which one. Neither are we.

cards.text: I can make the moon slightly bigger. For ambience. There may be tides in the high street.

right.label: Bigger moon
right.reaction: Gorgeous. Main Street is a beach on Tuesdays. Sal rents tyres as floats.

left.label: Normal moon
left.reaction: Normal moon. You're no fun. The moon agrees. It told me.

cards.text: The school science fair volcano works! Bad news: it's my volcano. It's real. It's in the gym.

right.label: Evacuate the gym
right.reaction: Everyone's out. The volcano is doing a small lava. Coach calls it cardio.

left.label: Give it first prize
left.reaction: It won. Timmy came second with a potato. Timmy hates the volcano now.

cards.text: My client requests a recess. Six hours. In a sunbeam. In your chair. Starting now. Lower your voice.

right.label: Give him the chair
right.reaction: He's asleep. You work from the floor now. It's honestly fine.

left.label: It's my chair
left.reaction: Noted. My client will now sit on your keyboard. 'jjjjjjjjjjjjjjjjjj'.

cards.text: Objection. The new council printer came in a box. My client claims the box. You may keep the printer.

right.label: He can have the box
right.reaction: Sustained. He's sitting in it. He has never been more powerful.

left.label: Box goes to recycling
left.reaction: My client has entered a hairball into evidence. On your desk.

cards.text: Marcel has written a noise complaint. It's forty pages. It's about the geese. And about you breathing.

right.label: Breathe more quietly
right.reaction: You did. You fainted. Marcel applauded. Silently.

left.label: Ask the geese to stop
left.reaction: Gerald replied with the loudest honk in recorded history. Marcel mimed dying.

cards.text: Marcel has been trapped in an invisible box in the square for nine days. People are worried. Is it real?

right.label: Send the fire brigade
right.reaction: They mimed cutting him out. He mimed thanks. Nobody knows if it worked.

left.label: Leave him, it's art
left.reaction: Tourists throw coins. Sal sells 'invisible box' T-shirts. They're blank.

cards.text: Marcel and Gerald are feuding. Marcel is miming a goose. Gerald finds it deeply offensive. Gerald is now miming a mime.

right.label: Separate them
right.reaction: Marcel mimed sorry. Gerald honked sorry. Peace, in silence and noise.

left.label: Sell tickets
left.reaction: Sold out. Gerald won on points. Marcel mimed a rematch.

cards.text: New menu! Every meal comes with a free tyre change. The tyres come with gravy. People love the gravy.

right.label: Back Sal
right.reaction: Queues round the block. Cars too. Some just want gravy on their wheels.

left.label: Food and tyres apart
left.reaction: Fine. Second restaurant next door. It's the same restaurant. There's a curtain.

cards.text: There's a badger in my kitchen. He wants a job washing up. He's already better than my staff. Is that allowed?

right.label: Hire the badger
right.reaction: Spotless plates. He's union now. Gerald signed him up.

left.label: Badgers can't work
left.reaction: He's gone. The dishes are filthy. My staff are celebrating. I hate them.

cards.text: Fitness is dropping, Mayor! Ten push-ups before every council meeting. Doug managed none. Doug fainted.

right.label: Push-ups for all
right.reaction: The council is stronger. Meetings are shorter. Too tired to argue.

left.label: Meetings stay seated
left.reaction: Coach blew his whistle at you for nine minutes. Your ears still ring.

cards.text: The geese want to play football against the town team. I've seen them train. Mayor, I'm scared. They tackle with necks.

right.label: Play the match
right.reaction: Geese 14, Town 0. Gerald scored with his face. Coach is in therapy.

left.label: Forfeit
left.reaction: The geese did a lap of honour anyway. Where did they get trophies?

cards.text: My crystal ball says: bury the town's money under a tree in the park. I've drawn a map. On a napkin.

right.label: Bury the money
right.reaction: Nobody can find the tree. The napkin got wet. 'It's there spiritually.'

left.label: Money stays in the bank
left.reaction: You'll regret it. She also said that about Tuesday. Tuesday was fine.

cards.text: Vision: you lose on Sunday. Unless you give me a pay rise. Then you win. Probably. The vision was blurry.

right.label: Pay rise
right.reaction: The vision is much clearer now. You'll win. Also there's a goose. There's always a goose.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Fine. Don't come crying to me when you lose. Unless you win.

cards.text: Gerald has hired Mr Whiskers. They're suing you for 'emotional honking damages'. Nobody knows what that means. Including them.

right.label: Settle with bread
right.reaction: One loaf. Two lawyers. Zero crumbs. Wing shook paw.

left.label: Fight it
left.reaction: Four-minute trial. Mr Whiskers fell asleep. Gerald honked. Dismissed. Probably.

cards.text: Gerald wants his own cookery show. Theme: 'bread, and how to steal it'. Episode one is called 'Your Bread'.

right.label: Commission it
right.reaction: Gerald's Kitchen is a smash. Nobody in town has any bread left.

left.label: No goose TV
left.reaction: He's filming it anyway on the library computer. Just honking. Huge numbers.

cards.text: Gerald would like a job interview. For your job. His CV is a slice of bread with 'HONK' written on it.

right.label: Interview him
right.reaction: He was very impressive. You've been demoted to Deputy Goose.

left.label: Reject the application
left.reaction: Gerald honked a formal complaint. In triplicate. Three honks.

cards.text: Parents' evening is tonight. All 400 parents want to talk to you personally. About the swings. There is one swing.

right.label: Build more swings
right.reaction: 400 swings. The park is just swings. Kids are bored of swings.

left.label: Talk to all 400
left.reaction: You finished at 4 am. You agreed to 400 things. Several contradict.

cards.text: The bake sale needs a judge. Last year's judge is still recovering. Bev has entered a cake with a firework in it. Lit.

right.label: Judge it bravely
right.reaction: You survived. Your eyebrows didn't. Bev won. Again.

left.label: Send Randy
left.reaction: Randy ate every cake, firework included. He's fine. He's glowing.

cards.text: I've bought the naming rights to Wednesday. It's 'ChadDay' now. Everyone has to say it. Happy ChadDay, Mayor.

right.label: Fine, ChadDay
right.reaction: ChadDay was a huge success. For Chad. Nobody else enjoyed ChadDay.

left.label: Wednesday isn't for sale
left.reaction: Then I'll buy Thursday. Thursday's cheaper. Nobody likes Thursday.

cards.text: I'm opening the Museum of Chad. Exhibits: baby Chad, Chad's first yacht, and Chad standing in a room.

right.label: Cut the ribbon
right.reaction: Opening day: six visitors. All Chad. In different hats.

left.label: No vanity museums
left.reaction: Fine. Museum of Not Chad. It's empty. It's very sad.

cards.text: I've put a speed camera on the duck pond. Ducks are doing nearly three miles an hour. Some of them are showing off.

right.label: Fine the ducks
right.reaction: We collected four crumbs and a feather. The ducks are appealing.

left.label: Ducks are exempt
left.reaction: They know they're exempt now. One did a wheelie. Ducks can't do wheelies.

cards.text: Sergeant Biscuit got promoted again. He's Inspector Biscuit now. He outranks me. He's ordered me to throw a ball.

right.label: Throw the ball
right.reaction: Inspector Biscuit is satisfied. You're on his commendation list. It's a sock.

left.label: Demote the dog
left.reaction: Biscuit filed a grievance. A long sad howl. The whole station is crying.

cards.text: The Bugle is giving you 'Most Mayor of the Year'. You were the only nominee. You still came second.

right.label: Accept graciously
right.reaction: Your speech ran in full. Including the minute where you just said 'um'.

left.label: Boycott it
left.reaction: 'MAYOR TOO SCARED OF AWARD.' Seven-page special. With diagrams.

cards.text: Small typo in today's Bugle. 'MAYOR {mayor} IS A GOOSE'. We meant 'GOOD'. Want a correction?

right.label: Print a correction
right.reaction: 'MAYOR NOT A GOOSE.' Gerald is offended. Gerald is suing.

left.label: Lean into it
left.reaction: You honked at a press conference. Approval up. The geese made you a member.

cards.text: I dropped the town calculator in the fountain. It only shows the number 7 now. I've done the whole budget with it.

right.label: Buy a new calculator
right.reaction: Budget fixed. We had money all along. Some of it was 7s.

left.label: Seven's a good number
left.reaction: Police budget: 7. Swings budget: 7 million. It's all 7 now.

cards.text: Can I have a day off? I keep crying at work. Not because of work. Because of a film about a dog. The dog was fine.

right.label: Day off
right.reaction: He saw the dog film again. He came back refreshed. And damp.

left.label: Cry at your desk
left.reaction: He did. The budget's soggy. Some numbers have run.

cards.text: Can I be mayor for one day? I've got a list. It's mostly 'everyone gets a dog' and 'no more Tuesdays'.

right.label: Mayor Timmy for a day
right.reaction: Everyone has a dog. Tuesday was cancelled. Nobody knows what day it is.

left.label: When you're older
left.reaction: I'll be nine next month. Then you'll see. THEN YOU'LL ALL SEE.

cards.text: Weather update: fog so thick I can't see the camera. Or myself. I'm not sure I'm here. Back to the studio.

right.label: Send a search party
right.reaction: Found Steve. Also two hikers and a bus that went missing in 1994. Still running.

left.label: Steve's fine
left.reaction: Steve's been missing three days. His forecasts keep coming. All 'fog'.

cards.text: The sun hasn't set in four days. I don't know why. I'm a weatherman, not a sun-man. Should I tell people?

right.label: Tell the public
right.reaction: Panic. Then barbecues. Then panic about the barbecues.

left.label: Keep it quiet
left.reaction: It set this morning. Nobody noticed. Everyone was finally asleep.

cards.text: A book came back to the library today. It was due in 1883. A ghost returned it. The ghost owes a fine.

right.label: Waive the fine
right.reaction: The ghost said thanks and borrowed another. Due back in 2160.

left.label: The fine stands
left.reaction: The ghost paid in very old coins. One is haunted. Doug is crying again.

cards.text: People say the library's 'Quiet Please' sign is too loud. 'Very shouty.' Should it whisper?

right.label: Make it smaller
right.reaction: Nobody can read it. The library is basically a nightclub now.

left.label: Make it LOUDER
left.reaction: QUIET PLEASE. Everyone left. Linda has never been happier.

cards.text: Hello again. I'd like to buy every hat in Bad Town. For hat reasons. Name your price.

right.label: Sell the hats
right.reaction: Everyone's head is cold. He's wearing all 4,000 at once.

left.label: Hats aren't for sale
left.reaction: Very well. I'll be back for the scarves.

cards.text: The {folk} want a vote on what they're called. Options: '{folk}', 'Bad Townsfolk', or 'Steve'.

right.label: Let them vote
right.reaction: 'Steve' won. Everyone is called Steve. Stormy Steve is upset.

left.label: The name stays
left.reaction: The {folk} accept this. Grumpily. Some now call themselves 'the Grumbles'.

cards.text: The bear is back. He's not causing trouble. He's in the library, reading about bears. He's upset about the chapter on him.

right.label: Give him a library card
right.reaction: He's borrowed 40 books. All about honey. Due back in spring.

left.label: Escort him out
left.reaction: He left a one-star review. 'Not enough bears.'

campaign.text: Election day. The town knows a goose won last time. Run on honesty, or run from it?

right.label: 'At least I'm not a goose'
right.reaction: Gerald heard. Gerald is at the window.

left.label: Promise a recount
left.reaction: Brave. If Gerald wins again we're moving.

up.label: Big rally
up.reaction: We ordered balloons. So many balloons.

campaign.text: Election day. One last push. What's the plan, boss? We believe in you. All three of us.

right.label: Big rally
right.reaction: We ordered balloons. So many balloons.

left.label: Attack ad about the cone
left.reaction: The cone did not respond. Classic cone.

up.label: Kiss every baby in town
up.reaction: Forty babies. One goose. It's fine.

objectives.text: Find out what is in the basement

low:people.title: Run Out by the PTA
low:people.text: Pam read out your record at a meeting. It took four hours. Nobody left. Then everybody came for you, with clipboards.

low:business.title: Bought Out
low:business.text: Chad bought City Hall, the chair you were sitting in, and the chair's opinion of you.

low:law.title: Arrested by Barb
low:law.text: Chief Barb arrested you for general crimes. The judge was Barb. The jury was Barb's helicopter.

low:press.title: Front Page Disgrace
low:press.text: The Bugle printed your face with the word NO under it. Every day. In bigger letters.

low:treasury.title: The Town Is Broke
low:treasury.text: The treasury is one button and a moth. Doug has gone to live in a tree.

high:people.title: Carried Off by Fans
high:people.text: The people love you so much they carried you out of town on their shoulders. They have not put you down.

high:business.title: Acquired
high:business.text: Chad loves you so much he bought you. You are now a subsidiary. Your title is Mayor (Brand Partner).

high:law.title: Made Permanent Deputy
high:law.text: Barb respects you so much she deputised you. For life. You live at the station now. There is a cot.

high:press.title: Turned Into a Column
high:press.text: Marge loves you so much she gave you a column. Then a second. Then you were the paper.

term:won.title: Re-elected
term:won.text: The town has spoken. Mostly in honks. Another week, heaven help everyone.

term:landslide.title: Landslide
term:landslide.text: Sixty per cent or more. The cone has retired. Gerald sent a card. It says HONK, but warmly.

term:lost.title: Voted Out
term:lost.text: The traffic cone will be sworn in at noon. It has promised to do nothing. People found that refreshing.

term:early.title: Recalled for Good
term:early.text: Three recalls. The town has filed you under Never Again. Randy has put the desk in a bin.

cliffhangers: Tomorrow: a pothole with a name.
Tomorrow: a note under your door. Very neat handwriting.
Tomorrow: Timmy has told everyone something.
Tomorrow: the basement. Bring a torch.
Tomorrow: the debate. Your opponent is orange.
